annotations.title: What a rate change would do to my numbers

description: Works out what a change in interest rates would do to someone's own variable-rate mortgage payment, HELOC interest, savings interest or GIC/CD renewal, to the cent, and which central bank drives that product (Canada: Bank of Canada; US: the Federal Reserve). Use it when someone asks what a cut or a rise would mean for them. Pure arithmetic on the numbers they give; for reference it also shows today's posted prime or GIC rate in Canada, or the US national average savings or CD rate. It never says whether a change will happen.

balance.description: Amount owed (mortgage, HELOC) or held (savings, GIC/CD), in dollars.

change_pts.description: The change to work out, in percentage points: -0.25 for a quarter-point cut, 0.5 for a half-point rise.

compounding.description: Mortgage only. Defaults to semi-annual in Canada, monthly in the US.

country.description: Where the product is. Decides which central bank it follows and, for mortgages, the usual compounding. Ask if unsure.

months.description: Mortgage: months left to pay it off (default 300). GIC/CD: the term in months (default 12).

rate_pct.description: The rate today, in percent a year.
